items.title: Skyrim lead chats about the Fallout diehards who hated that Bethesda got the series: 'We had to prove them wrong, and fortunately we did'
items.summary:
When Bethesda got its hands on the Fallout licence way back in 2004, the naysayers were many and vocal. In fairness, the naysayers are still many and vocal, but they were back then too, and it turns out Bethesda saw at least a few of their posts. In a chat with The Examined Game , Skyrim lead Bruce Nesmith reflected on the reaction some Fallout old-heads had to Bethesda's acquisition of the series.

"There was huge pushback when Bethesda got the Fallout licence to do Fallout 3. There was a lot of people who were Obsidian fans, who were like 'Bethesda's gonna screw it up, they're just gonna make it Skyrim, we want Fallout the way we remember Fallout', and there was a strong, vocal community that just hated that we were gonna make that game".

For clarity's sake, the angry fans at the time were likely Black Isle and Interplay fans rather than Obsidian fans—the latter studio hadn't ever made a Fallout game in 2004 (though it had Fallout alumni on staff), and they were prophesying (after 2006) that Bethesda's take on Fallout would be like Oblivion, not Skyrim, since the latter released in 2011. I suspect Nesmith is muddling the initial negative reaction with, well, the more modern one, which is shaped in large part by Obsidian's excellent Fallout: New Vegas from 2010.

"We had to prove them wrong", recalls Nesmith, "and fortunately we did, because Fallout 3 was embraced even by a lot of our sceptics". It's true: people bloody loved Fallout 3 and still do, though there are of course still series fans who reject the game. "There's always going to be some diehard people that say…
items.t: Skyrim lead chats about the Fallout diehards who hated that Bethesda got the series: 'We had to prove them wrong, and fortunately we did'

items.title: How to steal the BF Bandito in GTA 6
items.summary:
The BF Bandito is one of the many cars in GTA 6 that Moses asks you to steal and bring to him for cold, hard cash. This one has a search area out in Buskin Swamp, but when you arrive it's not immediately clear where or how to steal the car.

The owner of this white offroad racer will drive around the map marked search area in a circle, as shown in the clip above. To get him to stop, simply park your car blocking the track and stand next to it. When he reaches you, he'll slow down and call out, at which point you should press L2 to focus on him and use the "Mislead" dialogue option to ask for help.

In my version, Lucia was wearing a ski-mask and had a baseball bat, which quickly convinced them all to run away (after a few swings), but either way, once he stops it's easy to steal the car. The baseball bat probably wasn't necessary, but hey, it's still non-lethal.

As you exit the swamp, you'll get shot at and pursued by a few of his friends, but the BF Bandito is fast enough to outrun them easily. Bring it back to Moses to get $3,400ish as reward, though this may vary based on condition.

The leader of the operation reportedly commissioned a Guangzhou factory to produce the false Tifa and her ilk. They even sold some figures at higher prices than the genuine article, offering added accessories or features not available in the official product.

items.title: Blade Director Says He Walked Away From Marvel's Canceled Movie Because 'Life's Too Short to Make S**t Films'
items.summary:
Director Bassam Tariq has opened up about why he exited Marvel's Blade movie, saying, "life's too short to make s**t films."

The Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother filmmaker explained his reasoning for walking away from the Mahershala Ali superhero period piece during an interview with The New Arab . With just one other feature film (Mogul Mowgli) under his belt at the time, working on Blade presented quite the opportunity, but his short time attached as the flick's first director wound up being more of a learning lesson than anything else.

"It was funny and strange to start casting and building without a proper script," Tariq said when asked what working in the studio system taught him. "You're sitting there and explaining to actors what their role will be, and they just have to believe you.

"That's also very dangerous because if the text comes and it doesn't add up to what you were saying, your credibility gets completely shot. All I have is my integrity, and I've been thinking about that a lot."

Marvel Studios announced an Ali-led Blade film in 2019 and picked Tariq to lead the charge in 2021. A little more than one year later, and the director was said to have bounced off the project , with Marvel telling The Hollywood Reporter that "shifts in our production schedule" were to blame.

items.title: World of Warcraft: Forever has turned me into a big, friendly golden retriever that says hello to everybody
items.summary:
Terminally Online 

(Image credit: Future) This is Terminally Online : PC Gamer's very own MMO column. Every other week, I'll be sharing my thoughts on the genre, interviewing fellow MMO-heads like me, taking a deep-dive into mechanics we've all taken for granted, and, occasionally, bringing in guest writers to talk about their MMO of choice.

World of Warcraft: Foreve r's done a lot of things for me over the past couple of weeks—it's given me a deeper appreciation for oldschool MMO quest design, it's wowed me with some genuinely impressive new lighting technology, and it's… ugh, it's made me so friendly. 

Mind, I wouldn't say I'm unkind when I play MMOs, but I am a solo player by habit. I'll have a guild, friends I roleplay with, sure. But I'm very rarely striking up conversations with people in-game—all of that typically happens in Discord. And yet, here I am in WoW forever, trying to emphatically start conversations with goddamn everyone I meet.

And it's in part because of how much of a bastard the game is. I don't think Classic is a particularly difficult videogame—I've even gotten my warrior from level 1 to, at the time of writing, 56 as fury, a spec typically considered trash for levelling. And it's been fine, I've just minded my pulls and levelled first aid.

But it is a known fact that vanilla WoW quests are just easier when you group up with people. Part of this is because players are a force multiplier—many classes have group buffs, and not having to worry about health with a healer present means that you can pull swathes of enemies and melt them down easily.…

items.title: GTA 6 La Cascara Motel safe code
items.summary:
You'll need the GTA 6 La Cascara safe code if you decide to rob this tempting-looking ruined motel in Port Gellhorn. This is probably the most lucrative robbery in the town with an LMG, grenade launcher, and a unique weapon, plus a unique vehicle and a whole lot of drugs.

Thankfully, though, the safe code, which is 6969 (nice) is fixed for this robbery. As with the Brooks Boatworks safe code and the Bowling Alley safe code , you can actually find all three of these on a board in the Brooks Boatworks robbery in northwest Port Gellhorn. To find it:

Go to the east side of the compound. Go up the set of stairs into the grey building. Look at the map on the wall next to the whiteboard. Make sure to bring Jason to La Cascara when you can, since there's more than two stash bags worth of loot. Also, while you're on the top floor of La Cascara, head into the room next to the safe to find the Scrapped VF5C on the table—this silenced SMG is perhaps the best early gun I've found, simply because you can sneakily take out enemies. There's also a grenade launcher on the lower floor. 

As well as those, make sure to scour the top floor, the floor below it, and the first floor, for weed, pills, sticky bombs, and lots of cash. Finally, steal the Vapid Firebug Dominator (the red and black muscle car) out front to clear all the key valuables.

items.title: As a kid, I didn't have a monster in my attic, I had a LAN
items.summary:
Weird Weekend Weird Weekend is our regular Saturday column where we celebrate PC gaming oddities: peculiar games, strange bits of trivia, forgotten history. Pop back every weekend to find out what Jeremy, Josh, Rick and Ted have become obsessed with this time, whether it's the canon height of Thief's Garrett or that time someone in the Vatican pirated Football Manager .

Multiplayer gaming on PC these days is so easy you probably barely even think about it. Most games that support multiplayer will work out of the gate, and there's an abundance of ways to connect and chat with your friends across the globe. This is a far cry from the early days of PC multiplayer, when dial-up connections and ad-hoc servers made multiplayer PC gaming expensive and unreliable.

Indeed, the best way to play multiplayer PC games back then was via a LAN. A local network offered the fastest and most stable connections, and didn't cost you anything beyond the hardware required to hook it all together. Unfortunately, it was also the least convenient way of playing PC games with your friends, as it meant one or several of you had to haul your whole-ass PC to an agreed-upon location.

I will probably be in the ground when Bethesda finally releases The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel —which is kind of liberating. I have hype immunity. Tainted Grail is unabashedly created in the mould of The Elder Scrolls, in that it is a primarily first-person fantasy RPG where flexibility is its superpower. You chart your own course and effectively construct your class, enhancing skills by using them as much as possible. Opposite the Stash House The second wrecked Transgressor is further north in the garage of the house opposite the Kolt & Associate's Stash House robbery (there's a metal sunflower standing in the garden, which makes it easier to recognise.) It's also to the east of Brook's Boatworks and the west of Wasteland Offroad. Head around the side of the house via the driveway to find the car in an open garage at the back.

Behind Dirt Merchants This last one is nice and easy, behind the Dirt Merchants mod shop in the south of Port Gellhorn. It might sound odd for the developers of such a hugely successful game to be worried about losing their jobs, but layoffs don't just occur when games or companies struggle commercially. A common cause of layoffs in the games industry is companies trying to reduce overheads after a game has launched, as the studio switches from full production to post-release support for their current game and planning for the next one.

items.title: I didn't realize Etsy was selling bridges now
items.summary:
Online marketplace Etsy, best known as a platform for selling handmade goods, recently updated its user agreement to allow itself to "develop, train, test and improve artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies" using content uploaded by sellers.

This has not gone over well, with some closing their Etsy shops in protest. In response, Etsy has assured users that it doesn't plan to train AI systems designed to copy their work or replace their creativity. Instead, the company said that the change is about improving the platform and providing "services and tools that can help you run your business."

I am sometimes sympathetic toward companies that get yelled at for normal terms of service agreements. If a company hosts user-submitted content on the web, for instance, it needs a license to distribute that content globally, and sometimes users misunderstand that. This is not one of those cases.

The new agreement—which Etsy has told The New York Times it's planning to revise—says that Etsy and its third-party partners have the right to use uploaded content "to develop, train, test and improve artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies, including to improve the Services and/or help keep them safe."

That reads to me like blanket permission to train AI on user content for any purpose. The tacked-on note about keeping users safe does nothing to limit what Etsy can do.

The artists who sell cool custom keycaps and other fun things on Etsy are already likely to struggle against knock-off sellers if they get popular enough. That came with the territory…

items.title: NYT report documents ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's decades of berating employees: 'He said he would rip both arms off a subordinate and beat the person over the head to death with them'
items.summary:
It's been a strange couple of weeks for former Nvidia CEO, Jensen Huang. The once tech leader admitted to an affair, only for multiple affair allegations to surface , and he was then ousted from the company . Now, as he reportedly mounts a comeback, The New York Times has published a report detailing an alleged decades-long philosophy of getting more work out of employees "through humiliation". 

Reportedly, Huang told employees that they had become so rich that "he couldn’t motivate them simply with money", so the "only way he could grind more work out of them was through humiliation".

This method has reportedly been Huang's modus operandi for some time, with more than a dozen current and former employees claiming: "He has long used humiliation as a tool, excoriating employees in front of their peers with insults, personal attacks and violent comments, while telling them it was good for them or for the business."

That humiliation allegedly took many forms. One employee reported that Huang "said he would rip both arms off a subordinate and beat the person over the head to death with them. And he told another employee he would rip off the top of their head and 'pee on your brain'."

Two years ago, in a conversation with Stripe's Patrick Collison , Jensen Huang said, "I'd rather torture you into greatness, because I believe in you", and this behaviour appears to be an extension of that philosophy. 

Huang has apparently been called out for this behaviour. In the NYT report, Michael Winston, a former senior vice president of human resources, claims he threatened to sue…
items.t: NYT report documents ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's decades of berating employees: 'He said he would rip both arms off a subordinate and beat the person over the head to death with them'

items.title: Remembering the back alley brawls of The Warriors, a Rockstar city game that isn't an open world
items.summary:
The older I get, the more fascinated I somehow become by how videogames depict night, how particular technologies at particular times give rise to particular nightlives. I've already gushed about the Starlight Zone in Sonic the Hedgehog – the mild dissociation incubated by the soft, ceaseless glare of the construction yard, the eyeless brick at the level's nadir, the sleepless glitter of the skyline. Now, let me wind the clock forward, and backward, to Rockstar Toronto's The Warriors. One long night from the late '70s, sweaty and electric and menacing, fed through dank and sullen polygons from 2005.

Probably the best move Rockstar made with their adaptation of Walter Hill's film is to retain the element of phantasmagoria. Both the game and the movie open with a view of Coney Island's Wonder Wheel, its neon lamps forming a floating tracery of Morse code, cabins swinging almost imperceptibly against solid darkness. This is a kind of night in which light is more emblem than illumination, refusing to travel far, clinging to its source like a frightened ghost.
items.t: Remembering the back alley brawls of The Warriors, a Rockstar city game that isn't an open world

items.title: World of Warcraft: Forever isn't mere nostalgia bait - it's rebuilding the MMO social architecture that Blizzard spent years dismantling
items.summary:
I don't play video games regularly anymore. Not because I've lost interest in them, but because I no longer make the time, the premium on which has seemed to exponentiate with age. I realised, however, in 2019 that I was a kind of sleeper agent: whenever I heard the opening notes of Legends of Azeroth , the original World of Warcraft login screen music, I would feel the reactivation of a latent part of my mind laid down when I was 10 years old. And so, like a form of possession, whenever Blizzard announces a new legacy iteration of the original WoW, no downpayment in time nor money is too great to prevent me from returning.

Here I am, then, at the launch of World of Warcraft: Forever, seven years after Blizzard first revived the original 2004 game with World of Warcraft Classic in 2019. Once more I set foot on Durotar, to spend as much time as I can levelling up a new Orc Warrior before I am forcibly unplugged by either my boss or, more likely, my wife, and so far it's been a welcome return to some of the frictional - but more involving and consequential - socialising that WoW's decades of updates had previously sanded down.
items.t: World of Warcraft: Forever isn't mere nostalgia bait - it's rebuilding the MMO social architecture that Blizzard spent years dismantling

items.title: Korridor turns those Youtube ads for vertical mobile shooters into a new, "deeply strategic" genre, and I can't decide if it's lying
items.summary:
I like to think I'm difficult to hypnotise, but I confess, I'm a sucker for those Youtube adverts for the mobile vertical shooters. You know the ones: boglins pour towards an auto-firing player, who must dodge about to grab upgrades while whittling down the horde. The player in the advert always does pretty well for 20 seconds, but ahhhh, then they get just a tiny bit overconfident, mistime how long it'll take them to erode the health of an ogre midboss, and: bam!

Show me one of those ads, and I'll always watch to the end in the hope that this time, the protagonist will Study The Blade, conquer their harmatia, and slay the damn ogre. I've never actually played any of the mobile shooters in question, mind you. I'm far too cultured for that, you dope! Except that I've just been playing the demo for Korridor, which is supposedly "based off" of the ads, but might as well be one of the games they're promoting, for all I know.
items.t: Korridor turns those Youtube ads for vertical mobile shooters into a new, "deeply strategic" genre, and I can't decide if it's lying

items.title: I have double-checked and yes, original 'GTA killer' Driv3r really was that rubbish
items.summary:
At this point the tragedy of Driv3r , or Driver 3, or my personal favourite Drive-thrur, is well thumbed. A familiar litany of unrealised ambition, heinous bugs, dull open-world design, and an expensive yet audibly bored voice cast, the accidental comedic highlight of which is Michelle Rodriguez flatly reeling off car theft orders from what sounds like the inside of a Michelle Rodriguez-sized tupperware container.

A more widely forgotten detail is that, for a while, there was a non-zero chance - a belief, even - that Drive Three Er was going to be the opposite. The 2003-2004 hype cycle had sowed the notion that this would in fact be the open-world crime thriller to knock Grand Theft Auto off its perch, and even 22 years before GTA 6 's idolising reviews , that was no small promise; Rockstar were still enjoying the balmy success of Vice City, and we could see San Andreas cresting the hill on a stolen, shining BMX. "Ah, but did they have Michael Madsen doing doughnuts in car parks?," publishers Atari asked the world, either unaware or in denial of the spluttering, clapped-out rattletrap they were about to wheel into the showroom.

You likely know the rest, though one of the dangers of familiarity is the subsequent breeding of complacency, which in this case can manifest as a thawing acceptance. I succumbed to this myself, having recently installed a legally unlinkable copy of Drivethreeuh, mind opened to the possibility that maybe it wasn't that bad. Six hours later, I am here to tell you: it was.
items.t: I have double-checked and yes, original 'GTA killer' Driv3r really was that rubbish
